title: Canonical augmented cycle/object/outgoing-image rows
statement: Let A and B be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], let F:A -> B be additive and preserve finite limits and colimits, let K and L be integer-indexed cochain complexes, and let u:F(K) -> L be a complex morphism. Fix p in Z and bicomplex augmentations eI:single_0(K) -> I and eJ:single_0(L) -> J with natural-number resolution index [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Suppose the object, cycle and outgoing-image augmentation maps in horizontal degree p are quasi-isomorphisms, for both I and J. Put R_I=(Z^p(I) -> I^p -> image(d_I^{p,p+1})) and define R_J likewise; put G=F applied to resolution complexes. There exist short exact base rows S,T in B, augmentations a:single_0(S) -> G(R_I) and b:single_0(T) -> R_J whose three components are quasi-isomorphisms, a base-row morphism f:S -> T, and degree-zero identifications δ:single_0(S.X₁)^0 ~= F(Z^p(single_0(K))^0) and γ:F(K^p) ~= single_0(S.X₂)^0. They satisfy the following identities, in Lean composition order (≫): (1) a.τ₁^0 = δ.hom ≫ F((cyclesMap eI p)^0); (2) single_0(f.τ₁)^0 ≫ b.τ₁^0 ≫ (J.iCycles p)^0 = δ.hom ≫ F((single_0(K).iCycles p)^0) ≫ F(ρ_K.hom) ≫ u^p ≫ ρ_L.inv ≫ (eJ^p)^0; (3) F(ρ_K.inv ≫ (eI^p)^0) = γ.hom ≫ a.τ₂^0; (4) γ.hom ≫ single_0(f.τ₂)^0 ≫ b.τ₂^0 = u^p ≫ ρ_L.inv ≫ (eJ^p)^0. Here ρ_K:single_0(K^p)^0 ~= K^p and ρ_L are the standard singleObjXSelf identifications. This is only a row/augmentation presentation: it requires no injectivity and specifies no map between the resolution columns.

source.place: Lemma 015I (derived-lemma-cartan-eilenberg), alternating cycle/object/outgoing-boundary row; Remark 015K (derived-remark-functorial), naturality. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/015I and /tag/015K.

proof.text: Form the cycle/object/outgoing-image rows of the single bicomplexes on K and L. Specialize the proved kernel/image row lemma for an arbitrary HomologicalComplex in an arbitrary abelian category and arbitrary complex shape, with indices p,q satisfying c.next p = q, to q = p + 1. Its proof uses cyclesIsKernel and isKernelOfComp. Map the source row by F on resolution complexes, then evaluate both rows at zero to obtain short exact base rows.

Each column of a single bicomplex row vanishes in positive resolution degrees: for cycles use the monomorphic cycle inclusion, and for images use the epimorphic factorThruImage. F preserves zero objects. For a nonnegative cochain complex concentrated at zero, fromSingle₀Equiv constructs an isomorphism from the single complex on its zero term, with identity zero component. Apply this separately to the three columns; from_single_hom_ext gives the two row squares and ShortComplex.isoMk gives row isomorphisms.

Construct the row morphisms induced by eI and eJ using cyclesMap, the object components, and image.map. Their squares follow from cyclesMap_i and image.factor_map. Precompose the mapped source row morphism and the target row morphism with the row isomorphisms. Their six components are quasi-isomorphisms by exactness of F, the six hypotheses, and composition with isomorphisms. This constructs a and b; their cycle and object augmentation components at zero are the specified augmentation maps.

The middle base-row map is u.f p. Its composite from the source cycles to the target outgoing image is zero: cancel the monomorphic target image inclusion, use image.fac, u.comm, and the source iCycles_d equation evaluated at zero and mapped by F. The target short exact row lifts the source-cycle-to-target-object map to target cycles. The source short exact row descends the object-to-target-image map to its outgoing image. Their lift_f and g_desc equations construct f.

Take δ and γ to be identity isomorphisms on the zero components. The first and third identities are the computed zero components of a. The fourth follows from the definition of the middle component of f and the zero component of b. For the second evaluate cyclesMap_i for eJ at zero and combine it with lift_f for f.τ₁. The singleObjXSelf identifications at zero are identity isomorphisms.

proof_origin.place: F1: Tags 015I and 015K, canonical single-bicomplex rows; degree-zero evaluation, fromSingle₀Equiv, and kernel/cokernel universal properties replace explicit cycle/image preservation comparisons. Repair: generalize the private short-exact-row helper to arbitrary abelian categories and complex shapes, avoiding duplication of the private helper in the downstream object-stage module.

theorem exists_cartanEilenberg_comparison_augmented_rows
    {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} A] [Category.{v₂} B]
    [Abelian A] [Abelian B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) (L : CochainComplex B ℤ)
    (u : (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K ⟶ L) (p : ℤ)
    (I : HomologicalComplex₂ A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ))
    (eI : ((CochainComplex.single₀ A).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K ⟶ I)
    (hIcol : QuasiIso (eI.f p))
    (hIcycles : QuasiIso (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap eI p))
    (hIout : QuasiIso
      (image.map (Arrow.homMk' (eI.f p) (eI.f (p + 1)) (eI.comm p (p + 1)))))
    (J : HomologicalComplex₂ B (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ))
    (eJ : ((CochainComplex.single₀ B).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj L ⟶ J)
    (hJcol : QuasiIso (eJ.f p))
    (hJcycles : QuasiIso (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap eJ p))
    (hJout : QuasiIso
      (image.map (Arrow.homMk' (eJ.f p) (eJ.f (p + 1)) (eJ.comm p (p + 1))))) :
    ∃ (a : CartanEilenbergAugmentedRow ((cartanEilenbergCycleObjectRow I p).map
        (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ))))
      (b : CartanEilenbergAugmentedRow (cartanEilenbergCycleObjectRow J p))
      (f : a.base ⟶ b.base)
      (δ : ((CochainComplex.single₀ B).obj a.base.X₁).X 0 ≅
        F.obj (((((CochainComplex.single₀ A).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K).cycles p).X 0))
      (γ : F.obj (K.X p) ≅ ((CochainComplex.single₀ B).obj a.base.X₂).X 0),
      a.augmentation.τ₁.f 0 = δ.hom ≫ F.map ((HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap eI p).f 0) ∧
      ((CochainComplex.single₀ B).map f.τ₁).f 0 ≫ b.augmentation.τ₁.f 0 ≫
        (J.iCycles p).f 0 =
        δ.hom ≫ F.map
          (((((CochainComplex.single₀ A).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K).iCycles p).f 0) ≫
          F.map (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 (K.X p)).hom ≫
          u.f p ≫ (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf
            (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 (L.X p)).inv ≫ (eJ.f p).f 0 ∧
      F.map ((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 (K.X p)).inv ≫
        (eI.f p).f 0) = γ.hom ≫ a.augmentation.τ₂.f 0 ∧
      γ.hom ≫ ((CochainComplex.single₀ B).map f.τ₂).f 0 ≫ b.augmentation.τ₂.f 0 =
        u.f p ≫ (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 (L.X p)).inv ≫
          (eJ.f p).f 0
